title: Penguin Analysis Using R
text:
First, let’s load in the data about the Palmer Penguins; the first 6 rows are shown below.

library(tidyverse)
library(palmerpenguins)
head(penguins)

# A tibble: 6 × 8
  species island    bill_length_mm bill_depth_mm flipper_length_mm body_mass_g
  <fct>   <fct>              <dbl>         <dbl>             <int>       <int>
1 Adelie  Torgersen           39.1          18.7               181        3750
2 Adelie  Torgersen           39.5          17.4               186        3800
3 Adelie  Torgersen           40.3          18                 195        3250
4 Adelie  Torgersen           NA            NA                  NA          NA
5 Adelie  Torgersen           36.7          19.3               193        3450
6 Adelie  Torgersen           39.3          20.6               190        3650
# ℹ 2 more variables: sex <fct>, year <int>



How many islands do we have data for? Below, I count the unique names in the island column.

n_islands <- n_distinct(penguins$island)

n_islands

[1] 3



Let’s find the average flipper length by species. Below, I group the data by the values in the species column, and then calculate the average using the available flipper length measurements per species.

avg_flip <- penguins |> 
  group_by(species) |> 
  drop_na() |> 
  summarise(flipper_length_mm = mean(flipper_length_mm))
plot(avg_flip)




A figure showing average flipper length in mm by species





How about the average flipper length by species by island? I did the same thing as above, but this time also grouping by island.

avg_flip_per_island <- penguins |> 
  group_by(species, island) |> 
  drop_na() |> 
  summarise(flipper_length_mm = mean(flipper_length_mm))
avg_flip_per_island

# A tibble: 5 × 3
# Groups:   species [3]
  species   island    flipper_length_mm
  <fct>     <fct>                 <dbl>
1 Adelie    Biscoe                 189.
2 Adelie    Dream                  190.
3 Adelie    Torgersen              192.
4 Chinstrap Dream                  196.
5 Gentoo    Biscoe                 217.



It seems Adelie penguins on the island of Torgersen have slightly longer mean flipper length. Neat!

title: My first weeks in MDS
text: How I’m feeling. Photo taken by me.

title: My first weeks in MDS
text:
Orientation
Orientation was a fun way to meet my future classmates. Some information seemed redundant, but I suppose there was no way of avoiding that. Overall I left feeling supported and welcomed.

title: My first weeks in MDS
text:
The First Week
The first week was an uphill battle. I spent a lot of time in the labs and at home installing the software stack not once, but twice after I realized my Ubuntu setup wouldn’t work. This took away precious time from actually completing assignments. I also had to learn where all my classes were and how to use the software and do my assignments. However, it has been fun getting to know my classmates and figuring stuff out with them.

title: My first weeks in MDS
text:
How I’m Feeling Now
I’m tired! I have woken up before my alarm multiple times and not been able to go back to sleep because my mind automatically starts racing, thinking about due dates and how much I still need to do. The first week had also given me a false sense of security about commuting, because now that all other students have gone back to school, my commute time has increased by 30%. Hopefully these are growing pains. I am enjoying what I am learning.
